summary: Iteration 1 achieved a score of 69.5 (later refined to 78.9 with additional tuning), far exceeding the 33.5 baseline probe. The dominant factor is construction quality (grid-based nearest-neighbor accounts for ~93% of score), while simulated annealing with NN-guided 2-opt and single-city Or-opt adds ~5-8 points. The solution is now plateauing, likely stuck in local optima that simple SA moves cannot escape.
key_points: Iter-1 best score: 78.9 (vs 33.5 baseline probe and 64.5 NN-only). Grid-NN construction dominates; SA optimization contributes incrementally. The carrot/prime penalty structure accounts for ~1% of total cost, so prime scheduling is low-leverage.

Key unknown: Can double-bridge perturbation (non-sequential 4-opt) break the local optimum plateau? Standard TSP literature says yes, but the 2-second time limit constrains how many perturbation-restart cycles we can run on N=200K. Multi-city Or-opt (2-3 segments) and larger KNN (20 vs 12) may also help by finding moves single-city Or-opt misses.

Next iteration plan: Two arms — (1) h-main adds double-bridge perturbation + multi-city Or-opt + KNN=20 in an iterated local search loop, (2) h-ablation runs the same but without double-bridge to isolate its contribution. Target: score above 80. If both plateau at ~79-80, the next step would be LK-style moves or fundamentally different construction heuristics.
